title: Bij de huisarts
subtitle: At the doctor's
intro: After this lesson you can phone a GP practice, make an appointment and explain simple symptoms such as fever, a cough or dizziness. You can also understand and give simple advice, for example that you must drink and rest. You will practise the difference between al, nog and pas, and talk about how long you have been ill.

example.en: I am going to the GP.

words.note: Your regular GP in the Netherlands.
De huisarts is more common for your own GP.

grammar.title: Duration: al and sinds
grammar.explanation: Use **al** + a length of time for 'for': **Ik ben al drie dagen ziek.** Use **sinds** + a starting point for 'since': **Sinds maandag ben ik ziek.** Dutch uses the present tense here: **Ik ben al drie dagen ziek.** With **sinds** at the start, the verb comes second: **Sinds maandag ben ik ziek.**

rows: Ik ben al drie dagen ziek.
I have been ill for three days.
I have been ill since Monday.
Ik woon al twee jaar in Utrecht.
I have lived in Utrecht for two years.
Ik ben pas sinds gisteren ziek.
I have been ill only since yesterday.

grammar.title: al, nog, pas, nog niet
grammar.explanation: **Al** means 'already', **nog** means 'still' or 'yet', and **pas** means 'only' or 'just'. Put these words before the word you want to emphasise: **Ik heb al koorts.** **Ik ben nog ziek.** **Ik ben pas sinds gisteren ziek.** **Nog niet** means 'not yet': **Ik ben nog niet beter.**

rows: Ik ben pas sinds gisteren ziek.

grammar.tip: **al** = earlier than expected; **nog** = continuing; **pas** = later than expected; **nog niet** = not yet.

grammar.title: Moeten for advice
grammar.explanation: Use **moeten** + infinitive at the end to give advice: **U moet veel drinken.** **Je moet rusten.** The form **moet** is used for ik, jij, u, hij and zij (singular); **moeten** is used for wij, jullie and zij (plural).

examples.nl: U moet niet te veel werken.
examples.en: You must not work too much.

grammar.tip: The infinitive goes at the end: **U moet veel drinken.**

culture.title: Registering with a huisarts
culture.text: In the Netherlands, most people are registered with a local **huisarts**; this is the doctor you go to first for most health problems. When you phone the practice, the **assistente** often asks about your **klacht** and how long you have had it, so the doctor can decide how urgent it is. Outside opening hours, urgent help is arranged through a regional GP service; you usually phone first. Basic health insurance is compulsory, so you may need your **verzekering** details when you register.

summary: Make an appointment with **Ik wil graag een afspraak maken.**
Describe symptoms: **Ik heb koorts**, **ik hoest veel**, **ik ben verkouden**.
Talk about duration with **al** and **sinds**: **Ik ben al drie dagen ziek**, **Sinds maandag ben ik ziek**.
Use **nog**, **pas** and **nog niet** for 'still', 'only' and 'not yet'.
Give simple advice with **moeten** + infinitive: **U moet veel drinken en rusten.**
